item.title: would a Chernobyl SCP work?: Re: would a Chernobyl SCP work?
item.content:encoded:
would an SCP based on Chernobyl work nowadays?

Technically yes: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-4426 "SCP-4426 is the designation for a series of biological masses, located in and around the Chernobyl nuclear power plant and the nearby town of Pripyat."

We also have: http://www.scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-3204

So far as writing another Chernobyl SCP goes… not super likely to do well unless you have something extremely unique and unpredictable. There have been a lot of attempts at writing Chernobyl-based anomalies over the years; a forum-only search for "Chernobyl" will probably turn up plenty of concept and draft critique threads.

item.title: would a Chernobyl SCP work?: would a Chernobyl SCP work?
item.content:encoded: from what I understand SCPs based on real life places is no problem, but usually those places are either undefined beyond a general area or incredibly dangerous. Long story short I was thinking of making making an SCP based on Chernobyl, but from what I've researched Chernobyl has been open to the public for years now, would this make my idea pointless or could it still work?

item.title: Help: New writer who wants to create a canon.: Re: Help: New writer who wants to create a canon.
item.content:encoded:
Does it have to be a mix of tales and skips (like pitch-haven) or can it just be tales?

It can be just tales if you want (see e.g. bellerverse).

Also I feel obligated to point out here that Pitch Haven is a tale series which is a very different thing than a canon. Canons are intended as open, collaborative things where anyone can write within the canon, and you need to meet the 5 articles by 3 authors requirement for e.g. tags and stuff; whereas a tale series could be a solo thing produced entirely by you.

As a result, canons work best when they're settings over stories: e.g., broken masquerade is a canon where there's no veil and everyone knows the foundation and anomalies are real. However, if you're really wanting to tell a long story in multiple parts about this dude, a tale series is definitely better for you (and there's also, despite the name, no requirement to include only tales)

item.title: Help: New writer who wants to create a canon.: Help: New writer who wants to create a canon.
item.content:encoded: Alright, so I'm not exactly new to the SCP community, I've been a lurker for a while but never posted anything. But I have had this idea for a canon, in which a young man discovers that his estranged father is actually the creator/cause of a fair number of anomalies. For example (may or may not appear in future tales/skips) he was annoyed by a coworker and turned him into 106. But the problem is I'm not entirely sure how to make the canon work. I'm much more used to writing non-scp sci fi, so, I guess my main question is. Does it have to be a mix of tales and skips (like pitch-haven) or can it just be tales?

item.title: In need of help with refinement of SCP (Get. Keep. Shelter.): Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
Moved to Questions Desk since it's a query about part of the writing process, though authors really should not be making additional "advertisement" threads to ask for critique, as that generates spam.

Author, if you're having trouble getting further replies on a thread, you can look at this thread for options to contact reviewers: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

Please note that you can also use the IRC chatroom #thecritters to seek draft feedback without needing greenlights.
